question.problem:
Let be $f(x,y,z)$ a differentiable function such that

$$
\begin{aligned} & f(0,2,1)=8, & \, & {f}_{x}(x,y,z)=\frac{2{e}^{x}}{\sqrt{{e}^{x}+y+z}}, \\  & {f}_{y}(x,y,z)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{{e}^{x}+y+z}}, & \, & {f}_{z}(x,y,z)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{{e}^{x}+y+z}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(0,2,1),$ estimate the value of $f(-0.01,1.98,1.05).$
question.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b,c)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b,z-c⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(0,2,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(0,2,1)+∇f(0,2,1)\cdot ⟨x-0,y-2,z-1⟩ \\  & =8+⟨{f}_{x}(0,2,1),{f}_{y}(0,2,1),{f}_{z}(0,2,1)⟩\cdot ⟨x,y-2,z-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{x}(0,2,1)$, ${f}_{y}(0,2,1)$ and ${f}_{z}(0,2,1),$ using the given partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(0,2,1) & =\frac{2{e}^{0}}{\sqrt{{e}^{0}+2+1}}=1 \\ {f}_{y}(0,2,1) & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{{e}^{0}+2+1}}=1 \\ {f}_{z}(0,2,1) & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{{e}^{0}+2+1}}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
f(x,y,z)≈8+⟨1,1,1⟩\cdot ⟨x,y-2,z-1⟩.
$$

Finally, we can estimate $f(-0.01,1.98,1.05)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=-0.01,y=1.98$ and $z=1.05,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-0.01,1.98,1.05) & ≈8+⟨1,1,1⟩\cdot ⟨-0.01,1.98-2,1.05-1⟩ \\  & =8+⟨1,1,1⟩\cdot ⟨-0.01,-0.02,0.05⟩ \\  & =8-0.01-0.02+0.05 \\  & =8.02\end{aligned}
$$
